paper.title: Optimal Design for Active Preference Learning with Biased LLM Judges

settings.name_in_paper: Active preference learning with biased LLM judges (joint target-nuisance Bradley-Terry model, fixed design)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Non-adaptive optimal experimental design / parameter estimation problem (allocation fixed before outcomes); the performance metric is policy risk of a reward estimator, not cumulative or interactive bandit regret.
unmapped: two label sources: trusted human labels (Bradley-Terry with theta) and LLM-judge labels with logit X^T theta + W^T a (nuisance parameter a)
judge-deviation representation W is known/fixed (or learned from m historical units)
performance measured by KL-regularized policy loss D_F (Bregman divergence of log-partition value)
local asymptotic (root-n neighbourhood) analysis conditional on historical data
settings.definition_quote: We model the fixed judge preference probability q(z) ... q_{\theta,a}(z)=\sigma(X(z)^\top\theta+W(z)^\top a). Human labels follow the preference model p_\theta ... At type i, we collect n_i judge labels ... An independent trusted sample contains n_c human labels ...

algorithms.name: NAOD (Nuisance-Adjusted Optimal Design) with projected one-step estimator

bound.regime: n -> infinity, local minimax over root-n balls of radius R -> infinity

symbols.Phi_kappa: (1/2) tr(G_0 I_eff,kappa(xi)^{-1}), nuisance-adjusted policy-weighted design criterion

conditions: fixed allocation xi, conditional on historical data
T_n ranges over all reward estimators based on current observations

source.label: thm-local-policy-risk
source.quote: Fix \(\xi\) and condition on the historical data. Under the regularity conditions ..., suppose \(M_\kappa(\xi)\succ0\). If \(G_0\succ0\), then \lim_{R\to\infty}\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{T_n}\sup_{\|\eta\|\le R} n\,\mathbb{E}_\eta D_F(\theta_{n,h},T_n)\ge\Phi_\kappa(\xi)

results.notes: Quantity is policy risk E[D_F], a KL-regularized policy loss, not bandit regret. Scaled risk bound divided by n.

bound.regime: n -> infinity, uniformly over every fixed local ball

conditions: trusted-sample and initialization conditions of Appendix B.2
tuning: projected one-step estimator with guard constant c_s

source.label: thm-local-policy-risk
source.quote: Under the additional trusted-sample and initialization conditions in Appendix~\ref{app-minimax}, with \(\kappa>0\), the projected one-step estimator defined there attains this bound uniformly on every fixed local ball.

results.notes: Attainment part; actually n E D_F -> Phi_kappa (equality).

bound.regime: B -> infinity, uniformly over bounded local parameters

symbols.Phi_B: (1/2) tr(G_e M_B^{-1}) for the realized selected set of B distinct comparisons

conditions: conditional on historical data, candidate features and selected set
distinct-comparison regularity conditions of Appendix C.2

source.label: thm-distinct-comparisons
source.quote: Condition on the historical data, candidate features, and selected set. ... suppose \(M_B\) is uniformly positive definite. Under the local model \(\gamma_0+\eta/\sqrt B\), B\,\mathbb{E}_\eta D_F(\theta_0+h/\sqrt B,\widehat\theta_B)-\frac12\operatorname{tr}(G_eM_B^{-1})\longrightarrow0 ... If \(M_B\) converges to a positive definite limit, the corresponding conditional local minimax lower bound also holds.

results.notes: B here is the comparison budget, not knapsack budget. Statement also gives a matching local minimax lower bound when M_B converges (not recorded separately).

bound.regime: m,n -> infinity with n/m -> lambda_P in [0,inf); up to o(1/n + 1/m)

symbols.Phi_0: limit of oracle risk constant (1/2) tr(G_e M_m^{-1})
symbols.C_P: (1/2){tr(R_0 Sigma_P) + b_P^T R_0 b_P}, representation-learning cost
symbols.m_hist: number of historical units used to learn the judge-deviation representation

conditions: smallest eigenvalue of M_m bounded away from zero
sqrt(m) e_m converges in distribution to Z_P with mean b_P and covariance Sigma_P

source.label: thm-representation-cost
source.quote: Under the regularity conditions ..., suppose \(n_c/n\to\kappa>0\) and the smallest eigenvalue of \(M_m\) is bounded away from zero. Let \(m,n\to\infty\) with \(n/m\to\lambda_P\in[0,\infty)\). ... Then \mathbb E[D_F(\theta_0,\widehat\theta_{n,m})]=\frac{\Phi_0}{n}+\frac{C_P}{m}+o(n^{-1}+m^{-1})

results.notes: Asymptotic equality with o-remainder; recorded as exact leading-order expression.

symbols.Phi_dagger: (1/2) tr(G^dagger I_eff^{-1}) at the population root

conditions: regular estimator with asymptotically linear expansion M^{-1} U_n/sqrt(n)

source.label: prop:app-soft-sandwich
source.quote: n\,\mathbb E D_F(\theta_n^\dagger,\widehat\theta_n)\longrightarrow\Psi_{\rm soft}:=\frac12\operatorname{tr}(G^\dagger I_{\rm eff}^{-1}\Omega_{\rm eff}I_{\rm eff}^{-1}). If every row is additionally mean-correct, ... \Psi_{\rm soft}\le\frac12\operatorname{tr}(G^\dagger I_{\rm eff}^{-1}).

results.notes: Soft-feedback (bounded responses in [0,1]) variant; noise is bounded rather than Bernoulli here. Theorem A.4 shows the sup over such response laws equals Phi_kappa, attained by Bernoulli feedback.
